clue.text: Small group of Swedes getting Thursday as day of rest

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
ABBA, the Swedish pop group

explanation.surface: A Swedish band is pleased to be given Thursday off as their day of rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sabbath is the weekly holy day kept free from work in Jewish and Christian practice.

clue.text: Identifying feature of anaesthetist?

parts.note: an anaesthetist numbs patient after patient; read as one phrase it is the unique code stamped on an item

explanation.surface: What marks out a doctor who puts patients under?
explanation.walkthrough: Split the second word as NUMB-ER: one who numbs. An anaesthetist does it over and over, so is a serial one.
explanation.definitionFit: A unique code printed on a product or banknote is exactly what identifies that particular item.

clue.text: One senses pressure to exchange Italian capital for roubles

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means substituting it, so the capital takes the place of the currency letter

parts.note: to barter is to exchange goods
R is an abbreviation for roubles, the Russian currency
Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: A traveller feels pushed to swap Italian money for Russian currency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Italian capital' looks like money but is the city; it replaces the R inside BARTER.
explanation.definitionFit: This instrument measures atmospheric pressure, so it is a device that senses it.

clue.text: Refer everyone, vulgar Republican excepted

parts.note: all means everyone

indicators.note: excepted means left out, so the party letter is removed

parts.note: rude means vulgar

explanation.surface: Mention everybody except one crude Republican politician.
explanation.definitionFit: To allude is to refer to something indirectly, a near synonym in the sense of mention.

clue.text: Goodness, the French interrupt rudely

parts.note: heck is a mild exclamation like 'goodness!'
le is French for 'the'

explanation.surface: Exclaiming 'Goodness!', French people barge into a conversation.
explanation.definitionFit: Heckling is shouting rude interruptions at a speaker or performer.

clue.text: Meeting wartime captive? That's amazing

parts.note: POW is a prisoner of war
'wow!' is an exclamation of amazement

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a meeting with a prisoner of war.
explanation.definitionFit: A powwow is an informal conference or discussion, from a Native American gathering.

clue.text: Joke with philanthropist as matter of principle

parts.note: a pun is a joke on words
a donor gives money, as a philanthropist does

explanation.surface: A wisecrack shared with a generous benefactor is a matter of principle.
explanation.definitionFit: Pundonor is a Spanish-derived word for a point of honour, something one insists on out of principle.

clue.text: Weimar Republic extremists involved in genocide, for example

indicators.note: involved means tangled together, so these letters are mixed up
the extremists of a word are its outer letters, its first and last

explanation.surface: Political extremists in the Weimar Republic were implicated in genocide.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremists' looks like political radicals but takes the end letters R and C of Republic; these join WEIMAR in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: Genocide is an example of an atrocity counted under international law as an offence committed in conflict.

clue.text: Periodically, Joyce charms friar with razor

indicators.note: periodically means at regular intervals, so every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: Every so often, Joyce wins over a friar carrying a razor.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the second, fourth and so on letters of 'Joyce charms'.
explanation.definitionFit: William of Occam was a medieval friar, known for the principle of parsimony called Occam's razor.

clue.text: River joins another, far away from cities

parts.note: the Ural is another river, flowing from Russia into the Caspian

explanation.surface: One river flows into another in the remote countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Countryside areas lie away from towns and cities, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Agreement with Turkey's law

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for 'with'
TR is the international vehicle code for Turkey
an act is a law passed by a parliament

explanation.surface: A treaty is made according to Turkish legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: A contract is a legally binding agreement between parties.

clue.text: A durable role, possibly, for Corbyn?

indicators.note: possibly signals one possible arrangement of these letters among many

explanation.surface: A long-lasting position might suit Jeremy Corbyn.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeremy Corbyn headed the UK's Labour Party from 2015 to 2020, so the definition is by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Corbyn held the post of head of Britain's Labour Party, an example of the title.

clue.text: A right crazy sick old creature

parts.note: mad means crazy
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A truly mad, ailing, aged animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured burrowing mammal of the Americas, so an example of an animal.

clue.text: Strange Egyptian soul dance

parts.note: rum is an informal British word for strange
the ba was the soul in ancient Egyptian belief

explanation.surface: An Egyptian spirit performs an odd dance.
explanation.definitionFit: The rumba is a Cuban ballroom dance.

clue.text: Returning foreign visitor working for me?

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: ET is the extraterrestrial of the film, a visitor from another world
on means working, as a machine that is on

explanation.surface: An alien visitor going home is still working on my behalf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'me' (also spelt mi) is the third step of the tonic sol-fa scale, so it is a musical example; 'for' links.
explanation.definitionFit: In sol-fa singing, me is a name for one degree of the scale, an example of a musical tone.

clue.text: Army unit arriving half-cut at stag party?

indicators.note: half-cut means with half cut away, so only the first three letters stay

parts.note: coming means arriving
a stag party is a do just for men: a 'man do'

explanation.surface: Soldiers turn up drunk at a pre-wedding night out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it cuts COMING in half to COM.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a unit of elite assault troops, or one soldier in it.

clue.text: Abandoning its responsibilities, National Trust is retailing skimpy night attire

indicators.note: read as 're-tailing', it means giving the garment a new tail

parts.note: a negligee is a flimsy nightgown
NT stands for the National Trust, the British heritage charity

explanation.surface: A heritage charity selling flimsy nightwear has forgotten its duties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retailing' reads as RE-TAILING: the final E of NEGLIGEE is swapped for NT.
explanation.definitionFit: Failing to take proper care of one's duties is what being careless in this sense means.

clue.text: Site using hard work to process coca leaf

indicators.note: to process material is to work it into another form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A plant where labour converts coca leaves, a drug factory scene.
explanation.definitionFit: The coalface is where miners cut coal, and by extension any place of hard practical work.

clue.text: Sweat as Neuschwanstein's architect suggests how fee should be calculated

definitions.meaning: to sweat is to give off moisture through the skin

definitions.text: Neuschwanstein's architect suggests how fee should be calculated
definitions.meaning: Neuschwanstein is a Bavarian castle full of pointed towers

explanation.surface: A castle designer sweats over how to bill for his work.
explanation.definitionFit: Perspiring is the more formal word for sweating.

clue.text: Stammer badly describing love for Primate

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the scrambled letters encircle the zero
badly signals the letters are put in a bad, jumbled order

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O

explanation.surface: Someone stutters awkwardly while declaring love for an ape or monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round: the anagram of STAMMER goes round O.
explanation.definitionFit: The marmoset is a small South American monkey, so an example of a primate.

clue.text: It cooks royal jelly

parts.note: an Aga is a British range cooker

explanation.surface: A recipe line: something cooks royal jelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Agar is a gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to make jellies and culture media.

clue.text: End protest

definitions.meaning: an end is an aim or purpose, as in 'the end justifies the means'
to protest is to raise an objection

explanation.definitionFit: The noun sense is aim or goal; the verb sense is to voice disapproval.

clue.text: American agents about to be hiding in tree?

indicators.note: something hiding in another thing sits inside it, so the short word goes within the others

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency
ca, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: US spies are about to hide up a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to be hiding' reads as a phrase of intent; split it so 'about' is a piece and 'to be hiding in' the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The acacia is a thorny tree or shrub of warm regions, including the wattles.

clue.text: Organise quality boxing match

indicators.note: boxing means enclosing, so the words hold the answer within them

explanation.surface: Arrange a high-quality boxing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boxing match' looks like one phrase; 'boxing' is the indicator and 'match' alone the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To match something is to be its equal, as a verb or noun for a peer.

clue.text: Completely submerged by European articles

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article, a European one
der is the German definite article; 'European' covers both

explanation.surface: Someone swamped by items from Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fully beneath the water surface is said to be in that state, as a swimmer who goes down.

clue.text: Sign up Jules Verne?

definitions.meaning: to sign up for something is to enrol or put one's name down
Verne wrote about the submarine Nautilus, so he was a '...', a writer of subs

explanation.surface: Enrol the French novelist?
explanation.walkthrough: Split SUB SCRIBE: a scribe of the submarine novel Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To enrol for a magazine or service is to put one's name down for it.

clue.text: To glorify current understanding is ecstasy

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current
a deal is an understanding or agreement
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Praising the present consensus is pure bliss.
explanation.definitionFit: To idealise is to regard something as perfect, which glorifies it beyond reality.

clue.text: Doctrine of director associated with G Greene

definitions.meaning: a doctrine is a set of beliefs
Carol Reed directed films of Graham Greene's work such as The Third Man

explanation.surface: A film-maker's guiding beliefs, linked to novelist Graham Greene.
explanation.definitionFit: A creed is a system of religious or other belief, as is a doctrine.

clue.text: Stop releases by dictator

indicators.note: a dictator is one who dictates, speaking words for another to write down, so they are spoken

parts.note: frees means releases

explanation.surface: A tyrant's prisoner releases are halted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dictator' looks like a tyrant but is someone dictating, i.e. speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To freeze is to stop dead, or to hold prices or wages fixed.

clue.text: Kitchen device rotates liquid

indicators.note: liquid means flowing and fluid, so the letters move about freely

explanation.surface: A kitchen gadget spins fluid around, like a blender.
explanation.definitionFit: This electrical appliance browns bread, a standard piece of kitchen equipment.
